title: Mounts
description: Give the container a folder from the server, a volume that outlives its tasks, or a file written by the panel.

riskBadge.docker-socket: Exposes the Docker socket to this container
riskBadge.data-directory: Exposes the panel's data directory to this container

empty.title: Nothing is mounted
empty.description: Everything the container writes disappears with its task. Add a mount to keep it.

dialog.hostPathHint: An absolute path on this server.
dialog.name: Name
dialog.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits, dashes and underscores.
dialog.hostPathAdminOnly: Only an administrator can mount a path on the server.
dialog.mountPathHint: Where it appears inside the container.

deleteDialog.title: Remove this mount?
deleteDialog.description: {{path}} will no longer be mounted after the next deploy. The volume and its data stay on the server, even after the service is destroyed, until you delete them under Monitor, Storage.

risk.title: This gives the container power over the server
risk.mount_exposes_docker_socket: A container with access to the Docker socket can start containers of its own and take over this server. Only do this for software you trust completely.
risk.mount_exposes_data_directory: This folder holds the panel's database and its encryption key. A container with access to it can read every secret and change anything in the panel. Only do this for software you trust completely.

errors.hostPath: Use an absolute path such as /srv/app, with no . or .. in it.
errors.mountPath: Use an absolute path such as /data, with no . or .. in it. Docker can't mount over /, /proc, /sys or /dev.
errors.name: Use lowercase letters, digits, dashes and underscores, ending with a letter or digit.
